rubric.name: Hackathon judging
rubric.description: Four criteria, judged once by Jev; the aggregation decides the winner.
rubric.context:
You judge one hackathon entry from its write-up. Judge each criterion on its own: a strong entry can still score
low on one criterion. Most entries land in the middle.

levels.label: minor
levels.description: A small convenience for a few people

levels.label: useful
levels.description: A real problem for a clear group of people

levels.label: major
levels.description: A serious problem for very many people

levels.label: speculative
levels.description: Mostly unbuilt; the hard parts are unsolved

levels.label: partial
levels.description: A working core, with important parts missing

levels.label: proven
levels.description: Works end to end and is already used by real people

levels.label: familiar
levels.description: Works like many existing products

levels.label: fresh_angle
levels.description: A familiar idea with a new angle or audience

levels.label: new
levels.description: Nobody does this today

levels.label: sketch
levels.description: A mock-up or a prompt; little was built

levels.label: demo
levels.description: A working demo with rough edges

levels.label: polished
levels.description: A complete, polished build with real results

evidence.label: plant-pal.md
evidence.text:
# Plant Pal (fictional hackathon entry)
A chatbot that reminds you to water your houseplants and answers care questions. It uses a general chat model
with a plant-care prompt; reminders are set by hand. We demoed it on our own phones.
